title: What Technical Verification Methods Would Make Safety Properties Auditable? A Gap Analysis

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible with gap: cataloguing existing verification methods is a useful foundational step, but the gap taxonomy itself does not close any verification gap. The chain from taxonomy to improved auditability requires additional follow-up work.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Literature review and taxonomy construction are well within reach for CS students with guided mentorship. No specialized tools or advanced math required. 30 hours is sufficient for a focused review of a bounded set of methods.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Sustained effort required: cataloguing 'all existing technical verification methods' across formal verification, benchmarks, red-teaming, and interpretability is broad. Without strict bounding, scope can expand significantly.

novelty.reasoning: Largely addressed: multiple comprehensive surveys already catalogue technical verification methods for AI safety and identify auditability gaps.

novelty_assessment.label: largely_addressed
novelty_assessment.reasoning: This is heavily covered in recent literature. 'A survey of safety and trustworthiness of LLMs through the lens of verification and validation' (Springer AI Review, 2024) provides a comprehensive V&V survey. 'Towards Guaranteed Safe AI' (arXiv:2405.06624, 2024) proposes a framework combining formal verification, runtime monitoring, and interpretability. DeepMind published 'Towards Robust and Verified AI: Specification Testing, Robust Training, and Formal Verification'. The International AI Safety Report (2nd Key Update) covers technical safeguards and risk management. CISA published on AI red teaming as TEVV. 'Toward Verified Artificial Intelligence' appeared in CACM. The gap analysis between existing verification methods and auditability requirements is substantially covered by these surveys.
key_references: A survey of safety and trustworthiness of LLMs through V&V. Springer AI Review, 2024.
DeepMind. Towards Robust and Verified AI. Medium, 2019/updated.
